title: Data loss detection (DLP)
goal_html: Groups triage a batch of outbound transfer events, decide which are exfiltration alerts under a fixed DLP rule, and design an approved-destination list that would reduce false positives without missing real threats. Ties to LO 5.6.B.
steps_html:
1. Each group works through the the simulation egress queue, deciding ALERT or OK for each transfer against the >100 MB / non-approved-destination rule.
  2. The group lists every destination that appeared across all cases and sorts them into "should be on the approved list" vs. "should stay unapproved," with a one-sentence justification for each (is it an internal system, a known partner, or an unknown host?).
  3. Groups discuss: could an attacker deliberately keep transfers just under the volume threshold to avoid detection ("low and slow" exfiltration)? What additional signal (time of day, account baseline, destination reputation) would catch that?
collaborate_html: Assign roles: an "analyst" applies the fixed rule to each case, a "policy owner" curates the approved-destination list, and a "red teamer" argues how an attacker would evade the rule as written. Debate the red teamer's evasion case as a group.
exit_html: Each group submits: their final approved-destination list, and the one evasion technique the red teamer proposed plus a mitigation for it.
